title: I am in awe of Ali Louis Bourzgui’s talent but also of his immense br...
transcript: Like to say that theater is a form of escape, but I found more than ever that in this season, in time, that the theater is one of the last places people can come to worship the power of true, collective human presence. Amen. We take a moment to recondition our addiction to desensitization. We ask how we can see ourselves in a stranger's story and then carry that to the world that needs us to ask that more than ever. This is dedicated to the beautiful tapestry of immigrant families who make this country really special. May you one day not have to audition for the empathy that should be freely given by this country that benefits from your beauty. For the queer and trans communities who have and always will exist, no matter what people in power try to take away from them. To the people of Palestine, you deserve full life without occupation. For Eric Peter Maker, as an artist, may we continue to tell our stories and show our faces where humanity becomes undeniable and our families can no longer be written off as merely collateral damage. May they know the beauty of our kisses upon his cheek and the romance of a language rooted in passion for love and life itself. If there's one thing we can learn from vampires is that life is short. But that's his gift. Find beauty in the ephemeral and gratitude in what is not promised. And always invest in The people that want to see you blossom into your truest self and hold that space for them in return.
classificationReason: Creator expresses awe at Ali Louis Bourzgui (star of The Who's Tommy on Broadway) but the transcript appears to be a repost/reaction to his curtain speech (dedicated to immigrant families, Palestine, etc.), not the creator's own review of the production. No first-hand attendance or opinion about the show itself is expressed.
